failures.evidence: A stream that keeps its envoy_stream_id but stands behind a session's cursor drops the messages published after it, in silence. Live (sidm.sh, natscli v0.5.1): backup at last_seq 1; the session then saw 421..423, so its cursor was at 4. The session's NATS was cut, and the stream was deleted and restored from the backup (same id, last_seq 1). 424 was published, at seq 2. After the reconnect and 4 heartbeats: 0 cards for 424, 0 notices, cursor still at 4. The same happened when the stream was re-added from its exported config (sid3.sh: 415 and 416 at seq 1 and 2 with the cursor at 5, never shown). The engine resets on a cursor past last_seq only on the upgrade path; for a known id it trusts the cursor. Red test: 46751dc66075, `cd packages/envoy-client && bun test src/__tests__/replay.test.ts -t "keeps its id but stands behind a cursor"` -> FAIL (the message published after the restore is neither shown nor told).
